think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A young woman presents with a solitary cold, multilocular cystic thyroid mass in the complete absence of agricultural exposure or livestock contact. Cystic neck masses in euthyroid women are overwhelmingly managed as benign colloid cysts or cystic thyroid neoplasms, where fine-needle aspiration (FNA) is routine standard of care. However, primary thyroid echinococcal (hydatid) cysts are extraordinarily rare (<1% of all cases) and carry a catastrophic risk of anaphylactic shock and protoscolicidal seeding if aspirated with a fine needle.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Clinical history, thyroid examination, normal thyroid function and baseline laboratory tests, and non-invasive imaging (thyroid ultrasonography showing a lobulated cystic nodule with adjacent isthmic cysts, technetium-99m cold nodule, and negative abdominal ultrasound/chest radiograph) mark the admission breakpoint prior to the surgical subtotal thyroidectomy and histopathologic confirmation.
3. Differential Distinctions: Colloid nodule/cystic adenoma (typically lacks multiple adjacent daughter cysts or a thick distinct fibrous capsule separating cysts from parenchyma), thyroid carcinoma with cystic degeneration (typically exhibits solid papillary components, calcifications, or invasive features rather than well-circumscribed fluid cavities with internal daughter cysts), and parasitic hydatid cyst (Echinococcosis), which requires intact surgical enucleation or subtotal thyroidectomy without needle breach.
case_prompt: A 23-year-old woman, without any history of farming or raising livestock, presented with an enlarging neck mass that had been noticed 18 months before presentation. On physical examination, a well-circumscribed 3.0 x 3.0 cm mass was palpated in the right lobe of the thyroid, which was nontender on palpation. No cervical lymphadenopathy or other physical abnormalities were noted. Serum thyroid function tests as well as routine laboratory tests were within normal limits. An ultrasound study of the neck revealed a large lobulated cystic nodule in the right thyroid lobe with multiple adjacent cysts in the isthmus. A technetium-99m pertechnetate thyroid scan demonstrated that the lesion was a cold nodule. Abdominal ultrasonography and plain chest radiography revealed no focal visceral cysts or pulmonary lesions.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Colloid cyst / multinodular goiter with cystic degeneration
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Benign cystic nodules are the most common etiology of thyroid cystic lesions; however, high-resolution ultrasound demonstrated an atypical multilocular architecture featuring a large lobulated cyst with multiple adjacent isthmic daughter cysts, and gross operative inspection confirmed a thick fibrous wall delineating the cyst rather than simple colloid degenerating parenchyma.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: An ultrasound study revealed a large lobulated cystic nodule in the right thyroid lobe with multiples adjacent cysts in isthmus (Figure 1).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: A solitary cold thyroid nodule on technetium-99m scintigraphy in a young woman requires ruling out thyroid carcinoma; however, fine-needle aspiration was deliberately withheld due to clinical suspicion of an intact parasitic cyst to avoid fatal anaphylaxis and scolicidal spillage, and histopathologic examination showed no cellular atypia or malignancy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A technetium-99m scan demonstrated that it was a cold nodule.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot (Primary Thyroid Hydatid Cyst / Echinococcosis)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The sonographic appearance of multiple grouped cystic nodules without extrathyroidal lesions led clinicians to suspect echinococcosis and perform a subtotal thyroidectomy without needle biopsy, avoiding anaphylaxis; gross pathology and histopathology definitively confirmed hydatid cyst architecture with laminated membranes and fibrous encapsulation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Histopathologic examination confirmed the hydatic nature of the thyroid cyst (Figure 3).

editor_comments: Excellent fidelity case demonstrating primary hydatid cyst of the thyroid gland. Admission breakpoint cleanly excludes invasive surgery, intraoperative findings, and histopathology. Fine-needle aspiration was judiciously avoided to prevent scolicidal dissemination and anaphylaxis.
